pr_title: Add ability to hide played items in a feed
pr_body: #### What is it? - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Code base improvement - [ ] Meta improvement to the project #### Description of the changes in your PR - Let the user hide played items inside of a feed. - Use components from the new Groupie list library for displaying the feed list. - This allows for easier development of lists, and will make it easier to seamlessly update the list in the future (e.g. without blocking the view of the user with the loading progress). Fixes #3611 #### Testing apk The APK can be found by going to the "Checks" tab below the title and then on "artifacts" on the right.
pr_comments:
Question: Does this hide videos that have been only barely been started watching? (Like for a few seconds or minutes, or a few percent of total video time)

I know it hides stuff that a significant portion has been watched from the gif, but idk about that.

> Does this hide videos that have been only barely been started watching? 

I don't think so, this would require to change the way stream states are saved. Currently timestamps are only saved if at least `5s` into the video and (I think) `10s` before the end, but they should be saved always imo. Then it would be the player's job to start playing a video from the beginning when the saved stream state is `<=5s` or `>=(duration-10s)`. This would be a rather simple change, but  I think will go in another PR, unless @mauriciocolli wants to implement it here.

After testing on my phone I found some things that should be improved:
- the "eye" button should be shown in the app bar even when the "what's new" fragment is in a main page tab. It is inconvenient to have to click two buttons to access it. There are no space problems, and even if there where, it could just be shown as "ifRoom"
- When switching fast from the feed tab to another tab, the menu takes a little amout of time to reload, and during that time the three-dot menu can be opened, resulting in a gray square.
- The feed list updates are blocking the UI, and I only have 34 subscriptions. Have you tested the performance with hundreds of subscriptions? Anyway, can't list item filterings (i.e. dataset update) be done on another thread, while obviously keeping the list re-rendering on the ui one?

@Stypox 

> the "eye" button should be shown in the app bar even when the "what's new" fragment is in a main page tab. It is inconvenient to have to click two buttons to access it. There are no space problems, and even if there where, it could just be shown as "ifRoom"

> When switching fast from the feed tab to another tab, the menu takes a little amout of time to reload, and during that time the three-dot menu can be opened, resulting in a gray square.

The two are related, it looked very bad so I disabled it from the main page.

Though the second has nothing to do with this changes, the view pager seems to let the animation end to finally setup the menu, you can test it by instead pressing the tab's icon, it should be instantly changed.

I think it's possible to improve how fast it does that, but that's for another pull request.


> The feed list updates are blocking the UI, and I only have 34 subscriptions. 

I thought that the method that I was using did that, but apparently not. Fixed it.

> Have you tested the performance with hundreds of subscriptions?

Should not matter even if it had thousands, there's a limit to how many items are pulled from the database.
@mauriciocolli could you rebase, please? Then I would like to merge this.

I rebased this and tested a little bit, though I have not reviewed anything yet. @opusforlife2 @TiA4f8R @TobiGr @B0pol could you test the apk and check if everything works fine? Also, @Isira-Seneviratne, could you tell me if I did the correct things with the view binding? @mauriciocolli if you have some time could you check if I rebased correctly (especially the SQL part)?
I rebased again and also tested on API 19, everything works fine

@Stypox I don't use Watch History or Resume Playback regularly, so I could only give it a superficial sort of testing. It seems to work fine.

My only question is: why does it hide partially watched items? I can only imagine a user wanting to hide fully played items from a list. I don't see any use for hiding partially watched items. Did Mauricio provide any logic behind this design choice?
@opusforlife2 currently there is no way to check if a video was fully watched or watched for an instant, since progress is saved only if it is not near the progress bar edges.
@Stypox There don't seem to be any issues with the view binding code.

@Stypox But fully watched videos _do_ get hidden, while unwatched ones don't. If you were to also exclude partially watched videos, then the button's purpose would be properly served, I think.

Right now:
- Unwatched - not hidden
- Partially watched - hidden
- Fully watched - hidden

What I think the button should do:
- Unwatched - not hidden
- Partially watched - not hidden
- Fully watched - hidden

I'm not sure I get your point regarding "watched for an instant". As I've mentioned above, fully watched videos are already hidden by the PR. If it also hides "watched for an instant" videos, then I have a further question: does the app check if the item has an entry in the history database when deciding to hide it?

If so, I think "watched for an instant" videos should not get a history entry. Only if the seekbar is at the point where the progress would be saved (or the video ends) should it get a history entry. Would that solve the problem?

@opusforlife2 @mauriciocolli what do you think of this implementation? Now streams are hidden only if they are considered finished, and the red line under the thumnail is shown even for finished streams, so the "IN HISTORY" label is not needed anymore and was removed.

A video is now considered as finished if:
1. the time left until the end is less than ~~30~~ 60 seconds AND
2. the progress is at least 3/4 of the video length

Option 1. suits long videos (> 4 minutes). ~~I chose 30 seconds since youtube's end screens are 20 seconds long, adding to that the usual 10 seconds of bye-bye by the creator.~~ I chose 60 seconds since usually the sponsor, the bye-bye by the creator and YouTube's end screens take ~60s (e.g. see videos from "Two Minutes Paper" or by "Linus Tech Tips").
Option 2. suits short videos, that shouldn't be considered finished if only a small part was watched. I chose 3/4 of the video just because it seems reasonable to me ;-)

The stream progress is thus always saved (except if it is less than the first 10 seconds of the video), instead of not saving it if within the last 10 seconds like before, which prevented showing the red bar under finished videos.

@Stypox My bad. Finished videos weren't actually hidden in the version I tried. It just so happened that the couple of videos I tried it on were Shorts, which were 10-15 seconds long. Anyway, I'll try the new implementation and let you know.

Just tried it. A video was hidden even though progress was at 1:32/2:37. That fails both your conditions.

Tried another: 16:13/20:09. Result: hidden. Satisfies 2 but not 1.
Yet another: 0:06/0:20. Result: hidden. Fails both conditions.

- Rebased again @TobiGr @mauriciocolli 
- Increased the end threshold, used to consider a stream finished, to 60 seconds, since usually the sponsor, the bye-bye by the creator and YouTube's end screens take ~60s (e.g. see videos from "Two Minutes Paper" or by "Linus Tech Tips")
- Fixed stream state not being saved correctly at the end of a video (see https://stackoverflow.com/a/57848897/9481500)
- Probably also fixed stream progress not being correctly retained when switching players due to the point above
- Renamed `progressTime` to `progressMillis` for better understandability 
- Save stream state even if progress is less than 5 seconds, if the current time is more than 1/4 of the video length.
- @opusforlife2 please test again, I can't reproduce your problem above

- Rebased again @TobiGr 
- Do not hide feed buttons (show/hide & help) behind three-dot menu, instead make them visible `ifRoom`. This makes the eye button visible when the feed fragment is used in the main page, which is good in my opinion.
- Fix long-press menu and readd open-in-browser button

> please test again, I can't reproduce your problem above

@Stypox Seems to be fixed now. 👍

- applied the requested changes @TobiGr
- improved the two grid and list item layouts and fixed the related crash reported by @TobiGr 
- fixed group feeds not being updated correctly (no stream finished checks were present, so all streams that were opened at least once were hidden)
- reshow feed in `onResume()` if grid/list view mode changed in the settings

Every person that likes the former layout will find it a little better maybe. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Most of us can actually agree that after a subscription update we kinda can't know which videos has been added to the subscription feed. We have to remember which videos were there before an update to then figure out which videos were added. Especially when we have over 100 subscriptions and haven't updated in a few days.

Would it not be better to add something to display which new videos have been added?
comments:
> Every person that likes the former layout will find it a little better maybe.

Why?

> which videos were there before an update

You just have to remember the last video, since videos are always sorted by date.

Also, this would be fixed by #3371, wouldn't it?

@Stypox I like you, you're my favorite. Anyways. 

> Why?

I seriously don't know why xD. I love the new layout so I wouldn't be able to answer this question, but maybe?!

> You just have to remember the last video, since videos are always sorted by date.

Yes, sure, but that is exactly what this issue is about. Making it so people wouldn't have to remember the last video, this can be especially annoying when we have hundreds of subscribers or when one haven't updated in a while. And can't find the last video. Some channels upload multiple times a day and people can have a hard time figuring out where the newest video is in their feed.

> Also, this would be fixed by #3371, wouldn't it?

Not really, I don't usually watch every video that is uploaded. Most people have subscriptions that they just subscribe to because they wanna see what they upload. Like most of YouTube, (the inactive subscribers). Hiding only watched videos would only sort out those. And not by newly updated videos / old updated videos
Just having a separator ( **|** ) between the old videos and the newer videos would fix this issue really. But it isn't something major. Just a quick thought

This could also be extended. Even adding dates, like the original YouTube app. So it displays which day certain videos were uploaded on. But that would require it's own separate issue I guess ¯_(ツ)_/¯

can i suggest that we maybe make the text of the video a lighter shade if its from an "older" sync ? currently we have a red bar in the video thumbnail for progress, how about a tick in the middle to signify that a user has completely watched a video?  or even hide it like that PR?
@test2a Or a red line on the left side of the thumbnail to show new videos that resulted from the feed update.
